newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Sri Lankan navy destroys seven boats belonging to Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels off northeastern Kokkilai, killing more than 50 rebels.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga discusses welfare of Sri Lankan migrant workers in Kuwait during her two-day official visit to that country. Kumaratunga returned from Kuwait on Wednesday night.
Navy gun boats destroy seven LTTE boats off northeastern Kokkilai killing about 45 rebels including suicide cadres.

Court remands son of Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte till June 4 over killing of a Papua New Guinean rugby coach earlier this month, after Lohan Ratwatte was identified by witnesses at police identification parade.
Prime Minister Sirima Bandaranaike will fly to Beijing for medical treatment on Thursday.
Farmers in Sri Lanka's dry zone urge government to buy at least part of their dried chillie harvest, as market prices have tumbled due to low cost imports from India.
Troops of Operation "Jaya Sikuru" or "Sure of Victory" consolidate near the rebel-held town of Puliyankulam in the northern Wanni region after advancing slowly through stiff resistance.
